text: examples use eval = FALSE reference file paths replace data. example assumes 4D fMRI file (“bold.nii.gz”) corresponding 3D brain mask file (“mask.nii.gz”).
code: library(neuroim2)  # Read the fMRI data as a NeuroVec object using neuroim2::read_vec train_neurovec <- neuroim2::read_vec("path/to/bold.nii.gz", mode = "normal")  # Read the brain mask and create a NeuroVol object mask_vec <- neuroim2::read_vec("path/to/mask.nii.gz", mode = "normal") mask_vol <- NeuroVol(as.array(mask_vec), NeuroSpace(dim(mask_vec), spacing = c(2, 2, 2)))  # Create the MVPA image dataset real_dataset <- mvpa_dataset(train_data = train_neurovec, mask = mask_vol)  # Display dataset details print(real_dataset)

title: Contrast RSA with contrast_rsa_model
text: Standard Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) asks whether brain region’s representational geometry matches predicted similarity structure, typically returning single correlation value. powerful, approach tell aspects representational structure drive effect, individual voxels contribute specific theoretical dimensions. contrast_rsa_model() implements Multi‑Dimensional Signed Representational Voxel Encoding (MS‑ReVE) approach address limitations. MS‑ReVE decomposes local representational geometry user-defined contrasts—linear combinations experimental conditions capture theoretically meaningful dimensions. example, study four object categories, might define contrasts “animate vs. inanimate” “biological vs. mechanical” test whether conceptual dimensions spatially dissociable. method produces signed voxel-wise maps showing strongly voxel supports opposes contrast. Positive values indicate voxel’s pattern aligns predicted contrast direction; negative values indicate opposition. signed, contrast-specific information enables mechanistic interpretations standard RSA’s omnibus similarity measure. vignette walks compact example explains output metrics.

title: Contrast RSA with contrast_rsa_model
text: start generating small dataset defining two contrasts. Contrasts column‑centered: positive values indicate conditions pull voxel patterns one direction, negatives opposite direction.
code: # Generate dummy dataset (small 6x6x6 volume, 32 samples) set.seed(42) data_info <- gen_sample_dataset(D = c(6,6,6), nobs = 32, blocks = 4)  # mvpa_dataset object mvpa_dat <- data_info$dataset  # Define two contrasts across four conditions # Each row = condition, each column = contrast K <- nresponses(data_info$design) condition_labels <- levels(data_info$design$y_train)  C_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = K, ncol = 2) rownames(C_mat) <- condition_labels  # Contrast 1: conditions {1,2} vs {3,4} C_mat[1:2, 1] <- 1 C_mat[3:4, 1] <- -1  # Contrast 2: condition 1 vs condition 2 C_mat[1, 2] <- 1 C_mat[2, 2] <- -1  # Center each contrast (required for proper interpretation) C_mat <- base::scale(C_mat, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE) colnames(C_mat) <- c("AB_vs_CD", "A_vs_B")  # Visualize the contrast matrix print("Contrast Matrix (centered):") ## [1] "Contrast Matrix (centered):" print(round(C_mat, 2)) ##   AB_vs_CD A_vs_B ## a        1      1 ## b        1     -1 ## c       -1      0 ## d       -1      0 ## e        0      0 ## attr(,"scaled:center") ## [1] 0 0 ms_des <- msreve_design(data_info$design, contrast_matrix = C_mat)

title: Running Custom Analyses with rMVPA
text: First, generate sample volumetric dataset define custom function.
code: # Generate sample dataset (e.g., 10x10x10 volume, 50 observations, 2 blocks) dset_info <- gen_sample_dataset(D = c(10, 10, 10), nobs = 50, blocks = 2, nlevels=2) dataset_obj <- dset_info$dataset  # Define our custom analysis function # It calculates mean, sd, and number of features (voxels) calculate_roi_stats <- function(data, info) {   # Inputs:   # data: matrix (samples x features) for the current ROI/sphere   # info: list with id/center_index and feature indices      # Perform calculations   mean_signal <- mean(data, na.rm = TRUE)   sd_signal <- sd(data, na.rm = TRUE)   num_features <- ncol(data)      # Return results as a named list of scalars   list(     mean_signal = mean_signal,     sd_signal = sd_signal,     n_features = num_features   ) }  # Define a version that might fail for small ROIs/spheres calculate_roi_stats_robust <- function(data, info) {     if (ncol(data) < 5) {         stop("Too few features (< 5) in this region!")     }     # If enough features, proceed as normal     mean_signal <- mean(data, na.rm = TRUE)     sd_signal <- sd(data, na.rm = TRUE)     num_features <- ncol(data)     list(         mean_signal = mean_signal,         sd_signal = sd_signal,         n_features = num_features     ) }

code: # Create a region mask with 4 ROIs covering parts of the dataset mask mask_vol <- dataset_obj$mask mask_arr <- array(0, dim(mask_vol)) active_indices <- which(mask_vol > 0) n_active <- length(active_indices)  # Assign active voxels roughly to 4 regions set.seed(456) # for reproducibility roi_assignments <- sample(1:4, size = n_active, replace = TRUE)  # Make ROI 4 potentially small to test error handling roi_assignments[sample(which(roi_assignments==4), size=round(sum(roi_assignments==4)*0.9))] <- sample(1:3, size=round(sum(roi_assignments==4)*0.9), replace=TRUE)   mask_arr[active_indices] <- roi_assignments region_mask_vol <- NeuroVol(mask_arr, space(mask_vol))  # Run the custom regional analysis (sequentially first) custom_regional_results <- run_custom_regional(   dataset = dataset_obj,   region_mask = region_mask_vol,   custom_func = calculate_roi_stats,   .cores = 1,    .verbose = FALSE )  custom_regional_results #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>      id mean_signal sd_signal n_features error error_message #>   <int>       <dbl>     <dbl>      <int> <lgl> <chr>         #> 1     1    -0.00838     1.00         339 FALSE ~             #> 2     2    -0.0123      0.993        314 FALSE ~             #> 3     3    -0.00193     0.998        323 FALSE ~             #> 4     4     0.0232      1.02          24 FALSE ~  custom_regional_error_results <- run_custom_regional(   dataset = dataset_obj,   region_mask = region_mask_vol,   custom_func = calculate_roi_stats_robust,   .cores = 1,   .verbose = FALSE )  custom_regional_error_results #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>      id mean_signal sd_signal n_features error error_message #>   <int>       <dbl>     <dbl>      <int> <lgl> <chr>         #> 1     1    -0.00838     1.00         339 FALSE ~             #> 2     2    -0.0123      0.993        314 FALSE ~             #> 3     3    -0.00193     0.998        323 FALSE ~             #> 4     4     0.0232      1.02          24 FALSE ~

title: Running Custom Analyses with rMVPA
text: Next, run searchlight analysis using custom function. Explanation: output run_custom_searchlight searchlight_result list : - results: named list element corresponds metric returned custom_func (example, results$mean_signal, results$sd_signal) - metric element searchlight_performance object containing - $data: NeuroVol (NeuroSurface) holding metric values brain space - $summary_stats: basic statistics (mean, sd, min, max) across map values - related metadata like $metric_name, $n_nonzero - metrics: names metrics computed - n_voxels: total voxels/vertices defined mask - active_voxels: number voxels/vertices results values output maps ($data) represent result custom_func applied searchlight sphere centered voxel. “randomized” method used, map values represent average metric across spheres included voxel.
code:
# Run the custom searchlight analysis (standard method) # Use a moderate radius; set cores > 1 for parallel execution if available # Note: Running in parallel might print messages about the future plan setting. custom_searchlight_results <- run_custom_searchlight(   dataset = dataset_obj,   custom_func = calculate_roi_stats,   radius = 4, # e.g., 4mm radius   method = "standard",   .cores = 2, # Use 2 cores if available   .verbose = FALSE )  # Print the results object summary print(custom_searchlight_results) #>  #>  Searchlight Analysis Results  #>  #> - Coverage  #>   - Voxels/Vertices in Mask:  1,000  #>   - Voxels/Vertices with Results:  1,000  #> - Output Maps (Metrics)  #>   -  mean_signal  (Type:  searchlight_performance )  #>   -  sd_signal  (Type:  searchlight_performance )  #>   -  n_features  (Type:  searchlight_performance )  # Access the results for a specific metric (e.g., mean_signal) mean_signal_map_obj <- custom_searchlight_results$results$mean_signal  # The map itself is stored in the 'data' slot mean_signal_map_vol <- mean_signal_map_obj$data cat("
Class of the mean_signal map:", class(mean_signal_map_vol), "
") #>  #> Class of the mean_signal map: DenseNeuroVol cat("Dimensions of the map:", dim(mean_signal_map_vol), "
") #> Dimensions of the map: 10 10 10  # Print summary stats for the map print(mean_signal_map_obj$summary_stats) #> $mean #> [1] -0.007061025 #>  #> $sd #> [1] 0.0096284 #>  #> $min #> [1] -0.03503245 #>  #> $max #> [1] 0.03016657  # You can plot the map using neuroim2's plotting functions (example commented out) # plot(mean_signal_map_vol)

title: Running Custom Analyses with rMVPA
text: custom_func requirements: ensure function strictly follows input contract (roi_data/sl_data, roi_info/sl_info) returns named list single-row tibble scalar values. Inconsistent return types names across ROIs/spheres cause aggregation errors. Parallel Processing: Set .cores > 1 speed analysis. future package backend used. control, set future::plan() calling run_custom_* function (e.g., future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)). Error Handling: Errors occurring within custom_func specific ROI sphere caught automatically. analysis continue, affected ROI/voxel marked error flag contain NA output. Use futile.logger::flog.warn flog.error inside custom_func tryCatch blocks rMVPA detailed debugging messages. Memory: Searchlight analyses, especially large radii many randomized iterations, can memory-intensive. Monitor usage accordingly. Randomized Searchlight: using method = "randomized", ensure metric returned custom_func meaningful averaged across overlapping spheres.

title: Running Custom Analyses with rMVPA
text: custom performance function always receives single result object – typically classification_result – must return numeric vector scalar metrics (named return one): pass function mvpa_model() via performance argument: named entry my_perf() (accuracy, mean_pobs, max_pobs) becomes one volumetric map searchlight regional result.
code: my_perf <- function(result) {   # classification_result: result$observed, result$predicted, result$probs   acc  <- mean(result$observed == result$predicted)   pobs <- prob_observed(result)  # prob. of the true class for each trial    c(     accuracy    = acc,     mean_pobs   = mean(pobs),     max_pobs    = max(pobs)   ) } data <- gen_sample_dataset(   D = c(6, 6, 6),   nobs = 100,   response_type = "categorical",   data_mode = "image",   blocks = 4,   nlevels = 2 )  cval  <- blocked_cross_validation(data$design$block_var) mvdes <- data$design mod   <- load_model("sda_notune")  mspec <- mvpa_model(   model      = mod,   dataset    = data$dataset,   design     = mvdes,   crossval   = cval,   performance = my_perf )  res_sl <- run_searchlight(mspec, radius = 4, method = "standard") names(res_sl$results)

Metrics group run=1 suffixed "_run1", run=2 "_run2", . test set present, grouping indices interpreted design space mapped appropriate rows result via testind.
code: design_df <- data.frame(   Y   = rep(letters[1:2], 50),   run = rep(1:5, length.out = 100) )  mvdes <- mvpa_design(   train_design = design_df,   y_train      = ~ Y,   block_var    = ~ run,   split_by     = ~ run )  mspec <- mvpa_model(   model      = mod,   dataset    = data$dataset,   design     = mvdes,   crossval   = cval,   performance = my_perf )  res_reg <- run_regional(mspec, region_mask = data$dataset$mask) head(res_reg$performance_table)

title: ERA-RSA: Cross-Decoding Between Encoding and Retrieval
text: ERA-RSA model (era_rsa_model()) combines: Encoding–Retrieval Accuracy (ERA) — first-order similarity encoding retrieval patterns item, Representational Geometry — second-order similarity encoding retrieval representational dissimilarity matrices (RDMs). vignette walks small synthetic example encoding → retrieval cross-decoding using ERA-RSA, illustrates run regional searchlight analyses. ERA-RSA designed situations : encoding phase (e.g., stimulus viewing), retrieval phase (e.g., recognition recall), item key links encoding retrieval trials.

title: ERA-RSA: Cross-Decoding Between Encoding and Retrieval
text: start gen_sample_dataset() treat training split encoding external test split retrieval. row train_design test_design corresponds trial. item column links encoding retrieval presentations stimulus. toy data use paired row IDs item keys example one encoding one retrieval observation per item; applied analysis, column usually stimulus, image, word, event identifier design table.
code: set.seed(123)  toy <- gen_sample_dataset(   D            = c(4, 4, 4),  # modest volume for speed   nobs         = 24,   nlevels      = 3,           # 3 item categories   blocks       = 3,           # 3 runs   external_test = TRUE,       # required for encoding → retrieval   ntest_obs     = 24 )  # Add an item key column to both train and test designs item_keys <- sprintf("item_%02d", seq_len(nrow(toy$design$train_design))) toy$design$train_design$item <- factor(item_keys, levels = item_keys) toy$design$test_design$item  <- factor(item_keys, levels = item_keys)  head(toy$design$train_design) #> # A tibble: 6 x 4 #>   Y     block_var .rownum item    #>   <fct>     <int>   <int> <fct>   #> 1 b             1       1 item_01 #> 2 a             1       2 item_02 #> 3 a             1       3 item_03 #> 4 a             1       4 item_04 #> 5 c             1       5 item_05 #> 6 b             1       6 item_06

what: key_var vs y_train / y_test and phase_var
title: ERA-RSA: Cross-Decoding Between Encoding and Retrieval
text: mvpa_design already contains y_train / y_test, response labels trial (often category labels). ERA-RSA adds two extra notions: key_var: item key links encoding retrieval trials belonging underlying stimulus (e.g., image ID). ERA metrics era_top1_acc operate item level: retrieval trial ask whether top match among encoding trials key_var, just category. phase_var: phase label (e.g., encoding vs retrieval). external-test setup used , train split treated encoding test split retrieval, phase_var optional. required phases live image series. short, y_train/y_test describe shown trial (class/category), key_var defines item trial belongs ; ERA-RSA uses item keys build encoding–retrieval similarity geometry. combined series alternating encoding retrieval blocks, keep one design row per image volume identify phases explicitly: Pairing always key_var, never row adjacency block order. rMVPA splits image series internally preserving original observation order within phase.
code: era_ms <- era_rsa_model(   dataset = combined_dataset,   design = combined_design,   key_var = ~ item,   phase_var = ~ phase,   encoding_level = "E",   retrieval_level = "R",   pairing = "one_to_one" )

title: ERA-RSA: Cross-Decoding Between Encoding and Retrieval
text: build era_rsa_model run simple regional analysis small number regions. two similarity arguments operate different levels: distfun = cordist("pearson") says build within-phase RDM. Within region, ERA-RSA first averages trials key_var, computes one encoding RDM one retrieval RDM item-level patterns. rsa_simfun = "spearman" says compare two RDMs. second-order RSA step: lower triangle encoding RDM correlated lower triangle retrieval RDM. resulting regional metric geom_cor. external model RDM example. “model” second-order comparison encoding geometry : ask whether relative distances among encoded items preserved retrieval. performance_table contains one row per region several ERA-RSA metrics. Key metrics include: era_top1_acc — top-1 encoding→retrieval accuracy item key. era_diag_mean — mean encoding–retrieval similarity diagonal. era_diag_minus_off — mean item-specific similarity: retrieval item, matched similarity minus mean similarity nonmatching encoding items. complete similarities equals diagonal mean minus grand -diagonal mean. pairwise similarities missing, item estimable contrast receives equal weight. geom_cor — second-order correlation encoding retrieval RDMs. rsa_simfun = "spearman", rank correlation item-pair dissimilarities. quantify cross-decoding performance representational geometry alignment phases.

what: 4. When do you need ERA partitioning?
title: ERA-RSA: Cross-Decoding Between Encoding and Retrieval
text: ERA-RSA summary gives direct item matching raw geometry correlation. era_partition_model() asks sharper follow-question: much encoding-retrieval relationship uniquely explained -item transfer, much uniquely explained preserved representational geometry nuisance structure accounted ? makes useful single cross-decoding accuracy compressed. example, two regions similar top-1 accuracy, one may carry item-specific diagonal similarity another mainly preserves relative geometry among items. Read metrics layers: naive_top1_acc item-level direct-transfer score computed encoding--retrieval similarity matrix. xdec_Accuracy trial-level direct cross-decoding metric, matched prototype scorer used naive_xdec_model(). first_order_delta_r2 unique variance explained -item transfer cross-state similarity matrix. second_order_delta_r2 geom_cor summarize whether encoding item geometry preserved retrieval. random toy dataset, values near chance near zero. real data, region high first_order_delta_r2 weak second_order_delta_r2 supports item-specific reinstatement without much global geometry preservation. reverse pattern suggests relative arrangement items preserved even direct item identification weak. era_partition_model() can also include block, run, category, temporal, custom nuisance regressors item-level vectors item_block_enc, item_block_ret, item_run_enc, item_run_ret, item_time_enc, item_time_ret, item_category, plus first_order_nuisance second_order_nuisance. default, available item-level nuisance groups added automatically. Use auto_nuisance = FALSE use custom nuisance regressors, character vector auto_nuisance = c("run", "time") keep selected groups. enough paired items, set include_procrustes = TRUE add leakage-free orthogonal alignment decoder. include_procrustes controls optional decoder first learns orthogonal Procrustes map encoding prototypes retrieval prototype space. fit leave-one-item-: scoring item , rotation estimated paired items, held-retrieval item matched aligned encoding prototypes. gives Procrustes metrics procrustes_top1_acc, procrustes_diag_mean, procrustes_diag_minus_off. Use want ask whether encoding retrieval occupy representational space global rotation reflection. Leave small toy examples paired items stable held-alignment; min_procrustes_train_items sets minimum.

text: select_features() function applies feature selection process given feature matrix X response variable Y. function returns logical vector TRUE selected features FALSE otherwise. example using simulated data: Now, let’s use top_p option. select proportion features. example, cutoff value 0.1, top 10% features selected:
code: # Simulate a response variable (categorical) Y <- factor(rep(letters[1:4], each = 25))  # Simulate a feature matrix with 100 samples and 100 features X <- matrix(rnorm(100 * 100), nrow = 100, ncol = 100)  # Apply feature selection using the FTest method with top_k cutoff fsel <- feature_selector(method = "FTest", cutoff_type = "top_k", cutoff_value = 10) selected_features <- select_features(fsel, X, Y)  # The number of selected features should be equal to the cutoff value (10) cat("Number of selected features (top_k):", sum(selected_features), "\n") #> Number of selected features (top_k): 10 # Apply feature selection using the FTest method with top_p cutoff (select top 10% of features) fsel <- feature_selector(method = "FTest", cutoff_type = "top_p", cutoff_value = 0.1) selected_features <- select_features(fsel, X, Y)  # Calculate the proportion of features selected the_proportion <- sum(selected_features) / ncol(X) cat("Proportion of features selected (top_p):", the_proportion, "\n") #> Proportion of features selected (top_p): 0.1

code: set.seed(2026)  # Synthetic neural data: 50 trials in 4 blocks, small mask. sim <- gen_sample_dataset(D = c(6, 6, 6), nobs = 50, blocks = 4, nlevels = 2)  # Feature matrix shared across the simulation: 5 features driven by 2 latent factors. n_trials   <- 50 n_features <- 5 Z <- matrix(rnorm(n_trials * 2), n_trials, 2) B <- matrix(rnorm(2 * n_features), 2, n_features) F <- 0.7 * (Z %*% B) + 0.3 * matrix(rnorm(n_trials * n_features), n_trials, n_features) F <- base::scale(F) colnames(F) <- paste0("feat_", seq_len(n_features)) labels <- paste0("trial_", seq_len(n_trials)) mask_vol  <- sim$dataset$mask mask_idx  <- which(as.logical(neuroim2::values(mask_vol)))  datamat <- do.call(cbind, lapply(   neuroim2::vols(sim$dataset$train_data),   function(v) as.numeric(v[mask_idx]) ))  p1 <- rnorm(length(mask_idx)); p1 <- p1 / sd(p1) p2 <- rnorm(length(mask_idx)); p2 <- p2 / sd(p2) datamat <- datamat + p1 %*% t(0.5 * Z[, 1]) + p2 %*% t(0.5 * Z[, 2])  train_vec <- neuroim2::SparseNeuroVec(   datamat, neuroim2::space(sim$dataset$train_data),   mask = as.logical(neuroim2::values(mask_vol)) ) dset <- mvpa_dataset(train_vec, mask = mask_vol) design <- feature_rsa_design(   F        = F,   labels   = labels,   max_comps = 2,         # cap PLS/PCR components   block_var = sim$design$block_var )  cv <- blocked_cross_validation(sim$design$block_var)  mod <- feature_rsa_model(   dataset  = dset,   design   = design,   method   = "pls",      # PLS regression: F -> X   ncomp_selection = "blocked",   crossval = cv ) nvox <- sum(mask_vol) region_mask <- neuroim2::NeuroVol(   sample(1:3, size = nvox, replace = TRUE),   neuroim2::space(mask_vol),   indices = which(mask_vol > 0) )  res <- run_regional(mod, region_mask) res$performance_table #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   roinum pattern_correlation pattern_discrimination pattern_rank_percentile #>    <int>               <dbl>                  <dbl>                   <dbl> #> 1      1               0.285                  0.282                   0.756 #> 2      2               0.325                  0.336                   0.789 #> 3      3               0.251                  0.282                   0.738 #> # ℹ 6 more variables: rdm_correlation <dbl>, voxel_correlation <dbl>, #> #   mse <dbl>, r_squared <dbl>, mean_voxelwise_temporal_cor <dbl>, ncomp <dbl>

code: target_builder <- function(X_train, train_idx, builder_data) {   X_target <- builder_data$X_target   train_center <- colMeans(X_target[train_idx, , drop = FALSE])   source_center <- colMeans(X_train$X)   centered <- sweep(X_target, 2, train_center, "-")   sweep(0.85 * centered, 2, source_center, "+") } builder_design <- feature_sets_design(   X_train = da_example$design_fixed$X_train,   X_test = NULL,   block_var_test = da_example$block_var_test,   target_builder = target_builder,   target_builder_data = list(X_target = da_example$X_rec_noisy),   n_test = nrow(da_example$X_rec_noisy) )  builder_spec <- feature_rsa_da_model(   dataset = da_example$dataset,   design = builder_design,   mode = "coupled",   lambdas = c(low = 0.1, semantic = 0.1),   alpha_target = 0.3,   rho = 3,   rsa_simfun = "spearman" )  builder_res <- run_regional(builder_spec, da_example$region_mask)  builder_res$performance_table[, c("target_rdm_correlation", "target_r2_full")] #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   target_rdm_correlation target_r2_full #>                    <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1                  0.888          0.788

text: mvpa_model() reads classifier rMVPA’s pre-registered registry, swapping family one line. run VT analysis five classifiers covering different inductive biases: corclass — correlation--prototype, original Haxby (2001) method. naive_bayes — independent-feature Gaussian; simple baseline. rf — random forest (randomForest); ensemble bagged trees. svmLinear — linear support vector machine; large-margin separator. sda_notune — shrinkage discriminant; rMVPA’s recommended default. Cross-validated accuracy five classifiers, VT patterns leave-one-run-CV. Dashed line = chance 8-way problem (12.5%). sda_notune’s shrinkage discriminant dominates ≈25 percentage points. gap cross-validation artefact: leave-one-run-honest (fold’s 8 test patterns come single held-run; runs overlap; bundled mean patterns built per-run cross-run averaging leaks signal). Running sda::sda directly outside rMVPA patterns fold structure reproduces 0.917 two decimal places. wide spread? dataset shape (96 observations × 577 voxels × 8 classes) exactly regime pooled shrinkage covariance estimation pays : voxels strongly correlated, within-class covariance rank-deficient, unregularised methods either overfit (naive_bayes forced independence; rf averages weak high-variance trees) treat boundary geometrically without using covariance structure (svmLinear). corclass tops ≈27 % ’s 8-way correlation--prototype classifier; canonical Haxby (2001) ≈90 % numbers came binary, split-half-within-run version correlation classification structurally different 8-way leave-one-run-reported . full MVPAModels registry includes 22 classifiers; see ls(rMVPA:::MVPAModels) complete list vignette("FeatureSelection") adding feature selection inside CV loop.
code: fit_one <- function(model_name, ...) {   t0 <- Sys.time()   mspec <- mvpa_model(load_model(model_name), dataset = ds, design = mvdes,                       crossval = cval, ...)   res <- run_regional(mspec, region_mask, verbose = FALSE)   pt  <- res$performance_table   data.frame(     classifier = model_name,     accuracy   = round(pt$Accuracy, 3),     auc        = round(pt$AUC, 3),     seconds    = round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")), 1)   ) }  panel <- rbind(   fit_one("corclass"),   fit_one("naive_bayes"),   fit_one("rf",        tune_grid = data.frame(mtry = 50)),   fit_one("svmLinear"),   fit_one("sda_notune") ) panel <- panel[order(-panel$accuracy), ] panel #>    classifier accuracy   auc seconds #> 5  sda_notune    0.917 0.973     1.5 #> 4   svmLinear    0.698 0.853     2.1 #> 3          rf    0.500 0.694    10.4 #> 2 naive_bayes    0.375 0.481     1.7 #> 1    corclass    0.271 0.289     1.3

title: ITEM Trial-Wise Decoding
text: ITEM (Inverse Transformed Encoding Model) decoding trial-wise pipeline ROI searchlight analysis. Unlike standard MVPA, decodes single pattern per trial without accounting overlapping hemodynamic responses correlate trial estimates, ITEM makes trial-estimation step explicit corrects covariance induces. pipeline two stages: Trial estimation. least-squares-(LS-) GLM regresses TR-level data onto trial-wise design matrix X_t, yielding one response pattern per trial (Gamma). Covariance-aware decoding. nearby trials share overlapping HRFs, trial estimates correlated even underlying signals . ITEM computes trial--trial covariance U analytically X_t uses whiten decoder, evaluates leave-one-run-cross-validation. differs archived hrfdecoder pathway, fit continuous-time decoder directly TR-level data aggregated TR predictions events afterward. Reach ITEM want explicit trial-estimation stage direct control trial covariance handling, especially trial-level diagnostics. implementation delegates numerical work (item_build_design, item_compute_u, lsa, item_cv) fmrilss package, optional dependency.

title: ITEM Trial-Wise Decoding
text: key distinction standard mvpa_design supervised information lives trial level (T_target, length n_trials), data extracted per ROI/searchlight lives TR level (nrow(X_t) rows). Cross-validation folds derived internally trial-level run_id – specify block_var.

title: ITEM Trial-Wise Decoding
text: simulate small dataset, build trial-wise design, run regression decode three ROIs. Every ROI/searchlight location reports three scalars: item_score_mean – mean chosen metric across folds, item_score_sd – across-fold standard deviation, item_n_folds – number cross-validation folds (runs). random data correlation hovers near zero. real fMRI data, item_score_mean reliably zero (regression) chance (classification) indicates decodable trial-level structure.
code: set.seed(42)  n_time   <- 80   # TR-level observations n_trials <- 24   # trials to decode n_runs   <- 4  data_info <- gen_sample_dataset(   D = c(10, 10, 10), nobs = n_time, nlevels = 2, blocks = n_runs )  # Trial-wise design matrix: one column per trial (n_time x n_trials). # In real analyses this is built from your event onsets and an HRF. X_t    <- matrix(rnorm(n_time * n_trials), nrow = n_time, ncol = n_trials) run_id <- rep(seq_len(n_runs), each = n_trials / n_runs)  # Continuous trial-level target (regression mode). title: REMAP‑RRR — Domain‑Adaptive Cross‑Decoding
text: Classic cross‑decoding trains patterns one context (e.g., perception) tests another (e.g., memory). two domains rarely match exactly: recall patterns can systematically shifted relative perception. REMAP‑RRR now models memory “perception + low‑rank correction” jointly whitened space: Y_w ≈ X_w + λ X_w Δ, rank(Δ) ≪ p. Key points - Joint shrinkage whitening perception memory prototypes (stable small‑n, large‑p). - Residual reduced‑rank regression (RRR) learns Δ R_w = Y_w − X_w. - Automatic λ selection training items shrinks toward naïve cross‑decoder data weak. - Optional leave‑one‑key‑(LOKO) item’s adaptor diagnostics (e.g., R², improvement naïve) estimated item‑wise cross‑validated fashion. - Correlation classification predicted templates whitened space. LOKO vs single‑fit LOKO (leave_one_key_out = TRUE) primarily unbiased adaptor diagnostics item level. Test‑set classification metrics (accuracy/AUC external test set) always computed trials used fit adaptor, regardless LOKO setting. large searchlight runs adaptor diagnostics secondary speed critical, often reasonable set leave_one_key_out = FALSE use fixed rank, trading slightly optimistic adaptor diagnostics much faster single‑fit adapters per ROI. Note: complete introduction naive cross-decoding (baseline method), see vignette("Naive_Cross_Decoding"). vignette explains algorithm, use cases, domain adaptation needed.

NULL, pairing falls back class means.

title: REMAP‑RRR — Domain‑Adaptive Cross‑Decoding
text: regional result includes per‑ROI performance_table usual MVPA metrics new REMAP diagnostics: Standard metrics (classification): Accuracy, AUC (centered −0.5). remap_improv: fraction perception→memory mismatch explained vs naïve (0=gain, 1=perfect). lambda_mean: average λ selected training items (shrink toward naïve). delta_frob_mean: Frobenius norm λ·Δ (size learned correction). adapter_rank, adapter_sv1, adapter_mean_r2 remain completeness. return_adapter = TRUE (default), ROI row also carries rich predictor object inside classification_result containing diagnostic vectors. easiest way inspect call process_roi() single ROI examine result$predictor field. Key fields - r2_per_voxel: predictability target prototypes source (per voxel). - resid_by_item: LOKO residual (MSE) held‑key. - rank_by_item, sv1_by_item: RRR rank leading singular per held‑key. - keys_scored, skipped_keys: transparency LOKO fits. - sv_spectra_by_item: full singular spectra (optional; enable save_fold_singulars = TRUE).

title: REMAP‑RRR — Domain‑Adaptive Cross‑Decoding

title: Temporal Confounds in RSA
code: # Simulate a toy ROI RDM as a mixture of task + temporal + noise toy_roi <- scale(0.6 * task_mat + 0.3 * td_mat + matrix(rnorm(n*n, sd=.1), n, n)) diag(toy_roi) <- 0; toy_roi <- (toy_roi + t(toy_roi))/2  # Correlation before residualization v_roi  <- lower_tri(toy_roi) v_temp <- tvec cat(sprintf("Before residualization: cor(ROI, temporal) = %.2f\n", stats::cor(v_roi, v_temp))) Before residualization: cor(ROI, temporal) = 0.99 # Residualize ROI distances on temporal distances resid_roi <- stats::lm(v_roi ~ v_temp)$residuals cat(sprintf("After residualization:  cor(resid ROI, temporal) = %.2f\n", stats::cor(resid_roi, v_temp))) After residualization:  cor(resid ROI, temporal) = -0.00 # Visualize effect op <- par(mfrow=c(1,2), mar=c(4,4,2,1)) plot(v_temp, v_roi, pch=16, cex=.6, col="#444444",      xlab="Temporal distance (lower tri)", ylab="ROI distances (lower tri)",      main="Before residualization") abline(lm(v_roi ~ v_temp), col="#cc0000", lwd=2)  plot(v_temp, resid_roi, pch=16, cex=.6, col="#444444",      xlab="Temporal distance (lower tri)", ylab="Residual ROI distances",      main="After residualization") abline(h=0, col="#cc0000", lwd=2) invisible(par(op))

what: What problem does Vector-Based RSA solve?
title: Vector-Based RSA
text: Standard RSA correlates lower triangle neural RDM lower triangle model RDM gives one number per ROI. Vector-Based RSA something subtly different: trial correlates trial’s row neural distance matrix row reference distance matrix — trials blocks — returns one similarity score per trial. mean across trials becomes ROI’s rsa_score. per-trial framing buys three things: Built-across-block masking. Within-run pairs (suffer temporal autocorrelation, scanner drift, breathing, etc.) excluded automatically: trial , columns block_var != block_var[] used. Per-observation scores. return_predictions = TRUE get full vector trial-level RSA values, useful trial-level regressions, item-level analyses, single-trial QC. clean permutation null. Set nperm > 0 row-permutation null computed inside ROI, returning p_rsa_score z_rsa_score alongside mean.

title: Vector-Based RSA
text: Use Vector-Based RSA : one reference RDM (features, behaviour, model, prior dataset) want single, interpretable RSA score per ROI/searchlight centre. design runs/blocks want within-block comparisons excluded — default, opt-. want per-trial RSA scores can correlate behaviour single-trial covariate. want permutation-based p-value z-score without writing permutation loop . instead feature matrix want regression-style metrics (pattern correlation, R²) cross-validation, see vignette("Feature_RSA"). want fit multiple model RDMs competing predictors, see vignette("RSA").

title: Vector-Based RSA
text: Build design model: Run regionally ROIs: row one ROI; rsa_score average across-block second-order correlation.
code: set.seed(2026)  # Synthetic neural data: 50 trials in 5 blocks, small mask. sim <- gen_sample_dataset(D = c(6, 6, 6), nobs = 50, blocks = 5, nlevels = 2)  # A reference distance matrix derived from a feature space. n_trials   <- 50 n_features <- 5 F          <- matrix(rnorm(n_trials * n_features), n_trials, n_features) labels     <- paste0("trial_", seq_len(n_trials)) rownames(F) <- labels  D <- as.matrix(dist(F)) rownames(D) <- colnames(D) <- labels design <- vector_rsa_design(   D         = D,   labels    = labels,   block_var = sim$design$block_var )  mod <- vector_rsa_model(   dataset    = sim$dataset,   design     = design,   distfun    = cordist(),  # neural distance: 1 - Pearson correlation   rsa_simfun = "pearson" ) mask_vol <- sim$dataset$mask nvox     <- sum(mask_vol) region_mask <- neuroim2::NeuroVol(   sample(1:3, size = nvox, replace = TRUE),   neuroim2::space(mask_vol),   indices = which(mask_vol > 0) )  res <- run_regional(mod, region_mask) res$performance_table #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>   roinum rsa_score #>    <int>     <dbl> #> 1      1 -0.00647  #> 2      2 -0.0121   #> 3      3 -0.000355

title: Representational Mapping (ReNA-Map): repmap_model
text: ReNA-Map estimates low-rank linear map seed feature vectors (one vector per item) voxel patterns within ROI/searchlight. summarizes mapping rank, singular values, -sample variance explained (R²) per voxel. Inputs: item key, seed feature matrix (rows = items), fMRI trials grouped item Output (per ROI): map_rank, map_sv1/mean, map_r2_mean/median, map_frob_norm Implementation: reduced-rank regression (rrpack); falls back zero map rrpack installed, warning.

title: Representational Mapping (ReNA-Map): repmap_model
text: Many neuroscience questions ask: information one domain (e.g., semantic features, visual properties, computational model states) encoded neural activity? Traditional encoding models use full-rank regression, can overfit features outnumber observations. ReNA-Map uses reduced-rank regression : Discover intrinsic dimensionality feature→brain mapping (via map_rank) Prevent overfitting constraining mapping low-dimensional subspace Identify dominant encoding axes (via singular values) Example scientific questions: - many independent dimensions semantic space encoded anterior temporal cortex? - V1 use low-rank mapping Gabor filter banks (suggesting sparse coding)? - layers CNN best predict cortex, many principal components needed? Comparison alternatives: - vs. Full regression: ReNA-Map regularizes via rank constraint rather ridge/lasso penalties - vs. RSA: ReNA-Map models item-level patterns directly; RSA models pairwise distances - vs. PLS/CCA: ReNA-Map explicitly estimates coefficient matrix C prediction; PLS focuses latent variable correlation

title: Representational Mapping (ReNA-Map): repmap_model
text: minimal path uses small synthetic dataset single ROI built handful voxels.
code: library(rMVPA)  ## Synthetic dataset ds  <- gen_sample_dataset(D = c(6,6,6), nobs = 60, response_type = "categorical",                           data_mode = "image", blocks = 3, nlevels = 6)  ## Add an item identity column to group trials into item prototypes K <- 6 items <- paste0("I", 1:K) ds$design$train_design$ImageID <- factor(rep(items, length.out = nrow(ds$design$train_design)), levels = items)  ## Seed features (K x P) labeled by item P <- 8 seedF <- matrix(rnorm(K * P), K, P) rownames(seedF) <- items  ## Build design helper and model spec rpdes <- repmap_design(items = items, seed_features = seedF) rpmod <- repmap_model(dataset = ds$dataset, design = ds$design,                       repmap_des = rpdes, key_var = ~ ImageID,                       rank = "auto", max_rank = 5)  ## Define a small ROI (50 voxels) vox <- which(ds$dataset$mask > 0)[1:50] roi <- list(train_roi = neuroim2::series_roi(ds$dataset$train_data, vox), test_roi = NULL)  ## Per-ROI processing out <- process_roi(rpmod, roi, rnum = 1) out$performance[[1]]

title: Representational Mediation (ReNA-RM): repmed_model
text: ReNA-RM tests whether ROI’s representational geometry (mediator M) mediates relationship predictor RDM (X) outcome RDM (Y). reports standard mediation paths (, b, c′), total effect (c), indirect effect (·b), simple Sobel z/p. Inputs: item key, X Y RDMs (K×K), optional confound RDMs Output (per ROI): med_a, med_b, med_cprime, med_c, med_indirect, med_sobel_z/p

title: Representational Mediation (ReNA-RM): repmed_model
text: Key question: brain region actively transform relay information two representational spaces? Standard mediation analysis asks whether M mediates X→Y. Representational mediation extends similarity structures: - X: predictor RDM (e.g., semantic similarity word embeddings) - M: ROI’s neural RDM (computed voxel patterns) - Y: outcome RDM (e.g., behavioral similarity judgments) Example scientific questions: - hippocampus mediate relationship semantic similarity episodic memory confusion? (similar concepts get confused hippocampus encodes similarly?) - inferotemporal cortex transform low-level visual similarity (V1) categorical similarity (perirhinal cortex)? - brain regions along ventral stream actively reshape visual representations vs. passively relay ? Interpretation paths: - Path (X→M): predictor structure correlate neural geometry? (e.g., semantically similar words activate similar patterns?) - Path b (M→Y|X): neural geometry predict outcome similarity controlling predictor? (unique neural contribution) - Path c’ (X→Y|M): Direct effect predictor outcome removing mediation - Indirect effect (×b): much X→Y carried neural geometry? Comparison alternatives: - vs. RSA alone: RSA tests correlation; mediation tests mechanistic pathways - vs. Trial-level mediation: ReNA-RM operates representational geometries (2nd-order), revealing similarity structures transform across regions

title: Representational Connectivity (ReNA-RC): repnet_model
text: Key question: brain regions share representational geometry seed region computational model? ReNA-RC extension representational similarity analysis (RSA) adds: 1. Confound control: Partial nuisance similarity structures (temporal autocorrelation, low-level visual properties, task structure) 2. Functional connectivity representational space: Like seed-based connectivity, similarity structures rather timecourses 3. Multiple regression framework: Quantify unique variance explained seed vs. confounds Example scientific questions: - regions share hippocampal representational geometry controlling temporal proximity events? - posterior parietal cortex maintain categorical structure prefrontal cortex working memory? - visual areas correlate CNN layer N representations removing retinotopic confounds? Confound control examples: - Temporal lag RDM: Control autocorrelation (nearby trials similar regardless content) - Block RDM: Control slow scanner drift task-set effects - Low-level feature RDM: Isolate high-level representations removing pixel-level similarity confounds matter: Without confound control, might find “connectivity” ’s really just: - regions encode temporal context (content) - regions sensitive low-level features (abstract categories) - regions share task-evoked hemodynamic responses Comparison alternatives: - vs. RSA without confounds: ReNA-RC isolates unique shared geometry - vs. Seed-based connectivity: ReNA-RC measures similarity structure (geometry) rather amplitude covariation - vs. Searchlight RSA: ReNA-RC uses fixed seed (hypothesis-driven) rather whole-brain search

Arguments (key ones): - dataset: mvpa_dataset (train_data + mask) - design: mvpa_design (trial table) - key_var: column/formula giving item/key links encoding retrieval - phase_var: column/formula indicating phase (encoding vs retrieval) - encoding_level, retrieval_level: levels phase_var map E/R (default: first two levels) - distfun: distance function within‑phase RDMs (object shortcut handled create_dist()) - rsa_simfun: similarity comparing D_EE vs D_RR (“pearson”|“spearman”) - confound_rdms: optional named list K×K matrices dist objects item level - include_diag, return_item_scores, ... Key constructor steps: - Parse phase_var, key_var design$train_design via parse_variable helper. - Validate phase levels default encoding_level / retrieval_level supplied. - Normalize distfun distfun object. - Normalize confound_rdms square matrices row/col names matching item keys possible. - Call create_model_spec("era_rsa_model", ...) storing: dataset, design, parsed key/phase factors, E/R level labels, distfun, rsa_simfun, confound_rdms, flags, standard spec fields (compute_performance = TRUE, return_predictions = FALSE).

title: ERA–RSA Notes (Discussion 1)
text: ROI/searchlight, compute ERA metrics, geometry correlation, optional RSA regression confounds. High‑level steps: 1) Extract ROI data: X <- values(roi$train_roi) (trials × voxels); get indices. 2) Validate sizes; ensure phase key vectors (mod_spec) match nrow(X). 3) Build item prototypes per phase via group_means: - E_full <- group_means(X[enc_idx,], group = key[enc_idx]) - R_full <- group_means(X[ret_idx,], group = key[ret_idx]) - Intersect sort keys; subset E, R; require K ≥ 2. - Drop voxels zero variance across phases. 4) First‑order ERA (E×R): - S <- cor(t(E), t(R)) (rows = encoding items; cols = retrieval items; size K×K). - era_diag_mean <- mean(diag(S)). - ‑diagonal mean: set diag(S) <- NA; era_off_mean <- mean(S, na.rm = TRUE). - era_diag_minus_off <- era_diag_mean − era_off_mean. - Top‑1 matching accuracy: retrieval column, .max encoding rows compare identity index (seq_len(K)). Note: orientation E(rows)×R(cols). 5) Second‑order geometries: - D_enc <- pairwise_dist(distfun, E); D_ret <- pairwise_dist(distfun, R). - Vectorize lower triangles: dE, dR correlate method = rsa_simfun get geom_cor. 6) Optional geometry regression confounds: - Build vectorized predictors aligned common_keys: - Base predictor: enc_geom = dE. - confound RDM, subset common_keys vectorize lower triangle. - Optionally call check_collinearity(mm) available. - Fit lm(dR ~ ., data = .data.frame(mm)); extract non‑intercept betas beta_<name>. - run_lm_semipartial() exists, compute semipartial correlations; store sp_<name>. Return value: tibble columns - result = NULL (per‑trial predictions now) - indices = neuroim2::indices(roi$train_roi) - performance = list(c(n_items = K, era_top1_acc, era_diag_mean, era_diag_minus_off, geom_cor, beta_*?, sp_*?)) - id = rnum; error|warning flags + messages

code: #' Build item-level ERA-RSA confound RDMs from an mvpa_design #' #' @param design mvpa_design (same object you pass to era_rsa_model). #' @param key_var column name or formula giving the item ID (e.g. ~ ImageID). #' @param phase_var column name or formula indicating phase (e.g. ~ Phase). #' @param encoding_level(optional) encoding phase label; default = first level. #' @param retrieval_level(optional) retrieval phase label; default = second level. #' @param block_var(optional) column giving block/run membership. #' @param time_var(optional) column giving trial index or onset time. #' #' @return A list with elements: #'   - items: factor of item IDs used (only keys with both enc & ret trials) #'   - item_block: optional factor of per-item block labels #'   - item_time_enc, item_time_ret: optional numeric vectors #'   - item_lag: optional numeric vector (ret - enc) #'   - confound_rdms: named list of item-level RDMs (block/time-based) #' @export era_rsa_design <- function(design,                            key_var,                            phase_var,                            encoding_level  = NULL,                            retrieval_level = NULL,                            block_var = NULL,                            time_var  = NULL) {    assertthat::assert_that(inherits(design, "mvpa_design"))   d <- design$train_design    key   <- parse_variable(key_var,   d)   phase <- factor(parse_variable(phase_var, d))   phase_lev <- levels(phase)   if (is.null(encoding_level))  encoding_level  <- phase_lev[1L]   if (is.null(retrieval_level)) retrieval_level <- phase_lev[2L]    enc_mask <- phase == encoding_level   ret_mask <- phase == retrieval_level    block <- if (!is.null(block_var)) parse_variable(block_var, d) else NULL   timev <- if (!is.null(time_var))  parse_variable(time_var,  d) else NULL    # items with at least one enc and one ret trial   key_enc <- unique(key[enc_mask])   key_ret <- unique(key[ret_mask])   common_items <- sort(intersect(key_enc, key_ret))   K <- length(common_items)   if (K < 2L) warning("era_rsa_design: fewer than 2 items with both encoding and retrieval trials.")    Mode <- function(x) { ux <- unique(x); ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))] }    item_block     <- NULL   item_time_enc  <- NULL   item_time_ret  <- NULL   item_lag       <- NULL   confound_rdms  <- list()    if (!is.null(block)) {     item_block <- sapply(common_items, function(k) {       b_enc <- block[enc_mask & key == k]       if (length(b_enc)) Mode(b_enc) else NA     })     names(item_block) <- common_items      # same/different-block RDM (0 same, 1 diff)     B <- outer(item_block, item_block, FUN = function(a, b) as.numeric(a != b))     rownames(B) <- colnames(B) <- common_items     confound_rdms$block <- B   }    if (!is.null(timev)) {     item_time_enc <- sapply(common_items, function(k) {       t_enc <- timev[enc_mask & key == k]       if (length(t_enc)) mean(t_enc) else NA_real_     })     item_time_ret <- sapply(common_items, function(k) {       t_ret <- timev[ret_mask & key == k]       if (length(t_ret)) mean(t_ret) else NA_real_     })     names(item_time_enc) <- common_items     names(item_time_ret) <- common_items      item_lag <- item_time_ret - item_time_enc      # encoding-time distance RDM     Tenc <- outer(item_time_enc, item_time_enc, FUN = function(a, b) abs(a - b))     rownames(Tenc) <- colnames(Tenc) <- common_items     confound_rdms$time_enc <- Tenc   }    list(     items          = factor(common_items, levels = common_items),     item_block     = if (!is.null(item_block)) factor(item_block) else NULL,     item_time_enc  = item_time_enc,     item_time_ret  = item_time_ret,     item_lag       = item_lag,     confound_rdms  = confound_rdms   ) } era_des <- era_rsa_design(   design       = my_design,   key_var      = ~ ImageID,   phase_var    = ~ Phase,   encoding_level  = "enc",   retrieval_level = "ret",   block_var    = ~ Block,   time_var     = ~ Trial )  mspec <- era_rsa_model(   dataset       = my_dataset,   design        = my_design,   key_var       = ~ ImageID,   phase_var     = ~ Phase,   encoding_level  = "enc",   retrieval_level = "ret",   distfun       = cordist("pearson"),   rsa_simfun    = "spearman",   confound_rdms = era_des$confound_rdms,   # optional extras for block/lag metrics:   item_block    = era_des$item_block,   item_lag      = era_des$item_lag )

text: Patch snippets add computing S diag_sim:
code: # --- Block-limited ERA (if item_block is available) ------------------------ era_diag_minus_off_same_block <- NA_real_ era_diag_minus_off_diff_block <- NA_real_  if (!is.null(mod_spec$item_block)) {   # align item_block to the common_keys subset   ib <- mod_spec$item_block   if (!is.null(names(ib))) ib <- ib[match(common_keys, names(ib))] else ib <- ib[seq_along(common_keys)]    same_vals <- c(); diff_vals <- c()   for (i in seq_len(K)) {     same_idx <- setdiff(which(ib == ib[i]), i)     diff_idx <- which(ib != ib[i])     if (length(same_idx)) same_vals <- c(same_vals, S[i, same_idx])     if (length(diff_idx)) diff_vals <- c(diff_vals, S[i, diff_idx])   }    if (length(same_vals)) era_diag_minus_off_same_block <- mean(diag_sim, na.rm = TRUE) - mean(same_vals, na.rm = TRUE)   if (length(diff_vals)) era_diag_minus_off_diff_block <- mean(diag_sim, na.rm = TRUE) - mean(diff_vals, na.rm = TRUE) }  # append to perf perf <- c(perf,   era_diag_minus_off_same_block = era_diag_minus_off_same_block,   era_diag_minus_off_diff_block = era_diag_minus_off_diff_block )  # --- Lag-specific ERA (diag ERA vs E->R lag) ------------------------------ era_lag_cor <- NA_real_ if (!is.null(mod_spec$item_lag)) {   lag <- mod_spec$item_lag   if (!is.null(names(lag))) lag <- lag[match(common_keys, names(lag))] else lag <- lag[seq_along(common_keys)]   if (length(lag) == length(diag_sim) && any(!is.na(lag))) {     era_lag_cor <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(diag_sim, lag, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"))   } } perf <- c(perf, era_lag_cor = era_lag_cor)

text: computing D_enc, D_ret, vectors dE, dR: Notes: - already include run_enc/run_ret confound_rdms, beta/semipartial entries appear perf existing geometry regression. geom_cor_run_partial scalar complements reporting ER geometry jointly removing run structure phases. - Prefer encoding cross‑run ERA first‑order metrics feasible; second‑order controls provide symmetry.
code: # Run-partial ER geometry (residualize dE and dR on run confounds) geom_cor_run_partial <- NA_real_ if (!is.null(mod_spec$confound_rdms$run_enc) && !is.null(mod_spec$confound_rdms$run_ret)) {   Renc <- as.numeric(mod_spec$confound_rdms$run_enc[common_keys, common_keys][lower.tri(D_enc)])   Rret <- as.numeric(mod_spec$confound_rdms$run_ret[common_keys, common_keys][lower.tri(D_ret)])   conf_df <- data.frame(enc_run = Renc, ret_run = Rret)   dE_res <- stats::resid(stats::lm(dE ~ ., data = conf_df))   dR_res <- stats::resid(stats::lm(dR ~ ., data = conf_df))   geom_cor_run_partial <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(dE_res, dR_res, method = mod_spec$rsa_simfun, use = "complete.obs")) }  # Cross-run-only geometry (mask pairs sharing a run in either phase) geom_cor_xrun <- NA_real_ if (!is.null(mod_spec$item_run_enc) && !is.null(mod_spec$item_run_ret)) {   ire <- mod_spec$item_run_enc[match(common_keys, names(mod_spec$item_run_enc))]   irr <- mod_spec$item_run_ret[match(common_keys, names(mod_spec$item_run_ret))]   same_enc <- outer(ire, ire, "==")   same_ret <- outer(irr, irr, "==")   mask <- lower.tri(D_enc) & !(same_enc | same_ret)   if (any(mask)) {     geom_cor_xrun <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(D_enc[mask], D_ret[mask], method = mod_spec$rsa_simfun, use = "complete.obs"))   } }  # append to perf perf <- c(perf,   geom_cor_run_partial = geom_cor_run_partial,   geom_cor_xrun = geom_cor_xrun )

title: Improving Searchlight Error Handling (Proposal)
code: as_ok <- function(val, id, ctx = list()) {   tibble::tibble(     result = list(val$result %||% NULL),     indices = list(val$indices %||% NULL),     performance = list(val$performance %||% NULL),     id = id,     error = FALSE,     error_message = NA_character_,     warning = FALSE,     warning_message = NA_character_,     context = list(ctx)   ) }  as_err <- function(msg, id, ctx = list()) {   tibble::tibble(     result = list(NULL),     indices = list(NULL),     performance = list(NULL),     id = id,     error = TRUE,     error_message = msg,     warning = FALSE,     warning_message = NA_character_,     context = list(ctx)   ) }  bind_or_err <- function(x, f, id, ctx = list()) {   if (is.null(x) || inherits(x, "try-error")) {     msg <- if (inherits(x, "try-error")) as.character(x) else "Unknown error"     return(as_err(msg, id, ctx))   }   tryCatch(f(x), error = function(e) as_err(e$message, id, ctx)) }

title: Balance Cross-Validation Partitions — balance_partitions
text: **Sub-sampling (`method="subsample"`)**: 1. Identifies target class minimum number samples    (`min_count`) within set (train test). 2. *every* target class within set, randomly selects exactly    `min_count` samples *without replacement*. 3. Discards samples majority classes. **Oversampling (`method="oversample"`)**: 1. Identifies target class maximum number samples    (`max_count`) within set (train test). 2. *every* target class within set, randomly selects exactly    `max_count` samples *replacement*. 3. Duplicates samples minority classes. Balancing guarantees process, target class appears equally often within balanced training (optionally testing) set. useful preventing classifiers biased towards majority classes. output always `custom_cross_validation` object balancing process defines specific, explicit sets indices fold, may longer strictly adhere original blocking k-fold structure.

title: Grouped (banded) ridge domain-adaptation model (continuous predictors -> brain) — banded_ridge_da_model
text: Data model. ROI/searchlight, rMVPA provides: Train/source responses \(Y_{train}\) `dataset$train_data` (rows = TRs, columns = voxels). Test/target responses \(Y_{test}\) `dataset$test_data` (rows = TRs, columns = voxels). Predictors stored `feature_sets_design`: Train/source predictors \(X_{train}\) `design$X_train$X`. Test/target predictors either fixed \(X_{test}\) `design$X_test$X`,         fold-specific target predictors rebuilt `design$target_builder`. Grouped (banded) ridge. predictor column belongs named feature set (e.g. low/mid/high/sem). ridge penalty applied per-column based set, .e. diagonal penalty \(P\) entries columns set \(g\) take value \(\lambda_g\). Two training modes. stacked: fit single \(\beta\) stacking train test rows         (test -weighted `alpha_recall`/`alpha_target` optional test TR weights `design$X_test$row_weights`). coupled: fit \(\beta_{train}\) \(\beta_{test}\) coupling strength `rho`,         allowing controlled train->test shift still borrowing strength across domains. Test/target-time cross-validation (default). test blocks/runs provided (`design$block_var_test`) least two unique blocks, evaluation uses leave-one-block-test time. one block present, evaluation falls back contiguous folds test TRs (`recall_nfolds`/`target_nfolds`). cases, train TRs always included training fold. avoids transductive evaluation test data used training. Feature-set attribution via \(\Delta R^2\). `compute_delta_r2 = TRUE`, model computes leave-one-set-unique contribution held-test: $$\Delta R^2_g = R^2_{\mathrm{full}} - R^2_{-g},$$ \(R^2_{-g}\) obtained refitting model without feature set \(g\).

text: dataset object class mvpa_dataset, containing neuroimaging data associated metadata. design object class msreve_design, containing underlying mvpa_design contrast matrix. Created \link{msreve_design}. estimation_method Character string specifying method estimate cross-validated condition means (U_hat) distances. Supported: "average": Simple mean training samples per condition (U_hat). "L2_norm": Like "average", U_hat rows L2-normalized. "crossnobis": Computes unbiased cross-validated second-moment matrix independent partition means. preserves second-moment regression semantics "average" path removing -partition noise floor. Per-fold means crossnobis path averaged delta calculation. Requires `return_folds=TRUE` `compute_crossvalidated_means_sl`. Passed compute_crossvalidated_means_sl ("average", "L2_norm", get per-fold means "crossnobis"). regression_type Character string specifying method RSA regression (regressing empirical RDM/Second Moment Matrix onto contrast RDMs). Options align rsa_model: "pearson", "spearman", "lm", "rfit". Additional options ridge regression: "ridge_hkb" (Hoerl-Kennard-Baldwin lambda). Default "lm". output_metric Character vector specifying one output metrics compute. Multiple metrics can requested simultaneously returned named list. Duplicates removed preserving order first occurrence. Supported options: "beta_delta": product RSA regression coefficient (beta_q)         voxel's projection onto contrast (delta_q,v).         primary signed contribution metric. "beta_only": RSA regression coefficient (beta_q). "delta_only": voxel's projection onto contrast (delta_q,v). "recon_score": Voxel-specific RDM reconstruction score (r_v), correlating RDM implied voxel's loadings empirical RDM. "beta_delta_norm": Similar `beta_delta`, uses L2-normalized voxel contribution vector (delta_q,v). Requires `normalize_delta=TRUE` meaningful. "beta_delta_reliable": Reliability-weighted contributions, \(\rho_{q,v} \beta_q \Delta_{q,v}\), \(\rho_{q,v}\) reflects fold-wise stability. "composite": Sum beta-weighted, L2-normalized voxel contributions (sum q beta_q * delta_q,v). Represents net projection onto positive diagonal contrast space. Interpretation requires caution contrasts orthonormal. Default c("beta_delta"). check_collinearity Logical, whether check collinearity among contrast RDMs using regression_type = "lm". Default FALSE. normalize_delta Logical. TRUE, voxel contribution vector (delta_q,v) normalized unit L2 norm potentially multiplied beta_q "beta_delta" output metric. Default FALSE. allow_nonorth_composite Logical. FALSE (default) composite metric return NA contrast matrix orthonormal, avoid mis-interpretation. TRUE, composite score returned regardless, warning still emitted. calc_reliability Logical. TRUE, voxel-wise contribution reliability (rho values) estimated across cross-validation folds training can incorporated output metrics. Default FALSE. whitening_matrix_W Optional V x V numeric matrix (voxels x voxels). Supply `estimation_method = "crossnobis"` noise-normalized/Mahalanobis second moments desired. matrix (e.g., \(\Sigma_{noise}^{-1/2}\)) passed `compute_crossvalidated_means_sl` whiten per-fold estimates second-moment calculation. comparing implementations take precision matrix P directly, use W W %*% t(W) = P (example, `t(chol(P))` positive-definite precision matrix). Default `NULL` (Euclidean/-whitening Crossnobis). ... Additional arguments passed create_model_spec.

title: Constructor for contrast_rsa_model — contrast_rsa_model
text: model designed MS-ReVE style analyses goal understand different predefined contrasts contribute representational structure observed neural data, particularly fine-grained (e.g., voxel) level. involves: 1. Estimating cross-validated condition mean patterns (U_hat) partition means (Crossnobis). 2. Constructing empirical second-moment matrix (G_hat) U_hat using unbiased cross-validated second moment directly. 3. Creating theoretical second-moment matrices (RDMs) contrast vector. 4. Regressing vectorized empirical RDM/distances onto vectorized contrast RDMs get beta coefficients. 5. Projecting voxel patterns (U_hat) onto contrast space get delta values. 6. Combining beta delta form final output metric (e.g., beta_delta). **Cross-Validation Compatibility:** `estimation_method` relies `compute_crossvalidated_means_sl` , turn, requires cross-validation specification (`cv_spec` derived `mvpa_design$crossval`) provide deterministic, partition-based set training indices fold. Therefore, cross-validation schemes like `bootstrap_blocked_cross_validation` (use resampling replacement training folds) **suitable** use model, align assumptions `compute_crossvalidated_means_sl`. Schemes like `blocked_cross_validation`, `kfold_cross_validation`, `custom_cross_validation` (define clear partitions) appropriate. `twofold_blocked_cross_validation` `sequential_blocked_cross_validation`, compatibility also depends whether `train_indices` methods can deterministically define training sets fold iterated `compute_crossvalidated_means_sl`.

code: # --- Minimal Setup --- # 1. Create dummy data and an mvpa_dataset    # Dummy data: 16 samples, 10 voxels, 4 conditions, 2 runs   set.seed(123)   n_samples <- 16   n_voxels <- 10   n_conditions <- 4 # condA, condB, condC, condD   n_runs <- 2    dummy_array <- array(rnorm(n_voxels * n_samples), c(n_voxels, 1, 1, n_samples))   dummy_space <- neuroim2::NeuroSpace(c(n_voxels, 1, 1, n_samples))   dummy_sl_vec <- neuroim2::NeuroVec(dummy_array, dummy_space)    dummy_mask <- neuroim2::NeuroVol(     array(1, c(n_voxels, 1, 1)),     neuroim2::NeuroSpace(c(n_voxels, 1, 1))   )    condition_labels <- factor(     rep(paste0("cond", LETTERS[1:n_conditions]),         each = n_samples / n_conditions)   )   run_labels <- factor(rep(1:n_runs, each = n_samples / n_runs))    # Create mvpa_dataset (without Y and block_var)   mvpa_dat <- rMVPA::mvpa_dataset(     train_data = dummy_sl_vec,     mask = dummy_mask   )    # Create mvpa_design   mvpa_des <- rMVPA::mvpa_design(     train_design = data.frame(condition = condition_labels, run = run_labels),     y_train = ~condition,     block_var = ~run   )    condition_levels <- levels(rMVPA::y_train(mvpa_des))   K <- length(condition_levels)    C_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = K, ncol = 2)   rownames(C_mat) <- condition_levels   C_mat["condA", 1] <- 1; C_mat["condB", 1] <- 1   C_mat["condC", 1] <- -1; C_mat["condD", 1] <- -1   C_mat["condA", 2] <- 1; C_mat["condB", 2] <- -1   C_mat <- base::scale(C_mat, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)   colnames(C_mat) <- c("AB_vs_CD", "A_vs_B")    msreve_des <- rMVPA::msreve_design(     mvpa_design = mvpa_des, # Use mvpa_des here     contrast_matrix = C_mat   )    # --- Example 1: Basic contrast_rsa_model ---   model_basic <- contrast_rsa_model(     dataset = mvpa_dat,     design = msreve_des   )   print(model_basic) #>  #>  Contrast RSA Model Specification  #>  #> - Dataset  #>   - Class:  mvpa_image_dataset  #> - Design (`msreve_design`)  #>   - Name:  msreve_design_01  #>   - Contrast Matrix Dims:  4 Cond x 2 Contrasts  #>   - MVPA Design Class:  mvpa_design  #> - Analysis Parameters  #>   - Estimation Method (Uhat/d):  average  #>   - Regression Type (beta):  lm  #>   - Calc Reliability:      FALSE  #>   - Output Metric(s):       beta_delta  #>     # --- Example 1b: Requesting multiple metrics ---   model_multi_metric <- contrast_rsa_model(     dataset = mvpa_dat,     design = msreve_des,     output_metric = c("beta_delta", "recon_score", "beta_only")   )   print(model_multi_metric) #>  #>  Contrast RSA Model Specification  #>  #> - Dataset  #>   - Class:  mvpa_image_dataset  #> - Design (`msreve_design`)  #>   - Name:  msreve_design_01  #>   - Contrast Matrix Dims:  4 Cond x 2 Contrasts  #>   - MVPA Design Class:  mvpa_design  #> - Analysis Parameters  #>   - Estimation Method (Uhat/d):  average  #>   - Regression Type (beta):  lm  #>   - Calc Reliability:      FALSE  #>   - Output Metric(s):       beta_delta, recon_score, beta_only  #>     # --- Example 2: Using L2_norm for U_hat and normalize_delta ---   model_l2_norm_delta <- contrast_rsa_model(     dataset = mvpa_dat,     design = msreve_des,     estimation_method = "L2_norm",     normalize_delta = TRUE,     output_metric = "beta_delta_norm"   )   print(model_l2_norm_delta) #>  #>  Contrast RSA Model Specification  #>  #> - Dataset  #>   - Class:  mvpa_image_dataset  #> - Design (`msreve_design`)  #>   - Name:  msreve_design_01  #>   - Contrast Matrix Dims:  4 Cond x 2 Contrasts  #>   - MVPA Design Class:  mvpa_design  #> - Analysis Parameters  #>   - Estimation Method (Uhat/d):  L2_norm  #>   - Regression Type (beta):  lm  #>   - Calc Reliability:      FALSE  #>   - Output Metric(s):       beta_delta_norm  #>     # --- Example 3: Ridge Regression (HKB) ---   model_ridge <- contrast_rsa_model(     dataset = mvpa_dat,     design = msreve_des,     regression_type = "ridge_hkb"   )   print(model_ridge) #>  #>  Contrast RSA Model Specification  #>  #> - Dataset  #>   - Class:  mvpa_image_dataset  #> - Design (`msreve_design`)  #>   - Name:  msreve_design_01  #>   - Contrast Matrix Dims:  4 Cond x 2 Contrasts  #>   - MVPA Design Class:  mvpa_design  #> - Analysis Parameters  #>   - Estimation Method (Uhat/d):  average  #>   - Regression Type (beta):  ridge_hkb  #>   - Calc Reliability:      FALSE  #>   - Output Metric(s):       beta_delta  #>     # --- Example 4: Reconstruction Score Output ---   model_recon <- contrast_rsa_model(     dataset = mvpa_dat,     design = msreve_des,     output_metric = "recon_score"   )   print(model_recon) #>  #>  Contrast RSA Model Specification  #>  #> - Dataset  #>   - Class:  mvpa_image_dataset  #> - Design (`msreve_design`)  #>   - Name:  msreve_design_01  #>   - Contrast Matrix Dims:  4 Cond x 2 Contrasts  #>   - MVPA Design Class:  mvpa_design  #> - Analysis Parameters  #>   - Estimation Method (Uhat/d):  average  #>   - Regression Type (beta):  lm  #>   - Calc Reliability:      FALSE  #>   - Output Metric(s):       recon_score  #>     # --- Example 5: Composite Score Output ---   C_mat_ortho <- rMVPA::orthogonalize_contrasts(C_mat)   msreve_des_ortho <- rMVPA::msreve_design(       mvpa_design = mvpa_des, # Use mvpa_des here       contrast_matrix = C_mat_ortho   ) #> Warning: Contrast matrix has no rownames and mvpa_design$conditions is NULL. Assuming row order matches sorted unique condition labels from Y for block mapping.   print(paste("Is contrast matrix orthonormal:", attr(msreve_des_ortho, "is_orthonormal"))) #> [1] "Is contrast matrix orthonormal: TRUE"    model_composite <- contrast_rsa_model(     dataset = mvpa_dat,     design = msreve_des_ortho,     output_metric = "composite",     normalize_delta = TRUE    )   print(model_composite) #>  #>  Contrast RSA Model Specification  #>  #> - Dataset  #>   - Class:  mvpa_image_dataset  #> - Design (`msreve_design`)  #>   - Name:  msreve_design_01  #>   - Contrast Matrix Dims:  4 Cond x 2 Contrasts  #>   - MVPA Design Class:  mvpa_design  #> - Analysis Parameters  #>   - Estimation Method (Uhat/d):  average  #>   - Regression Type (beta):  lm  #>   - Calc Reliability:      FALSE  #>   - Output Metric(s):       composite  #>     # --- Example 6: Crossnobis estimation_method ---   # This shows the Euclidean crossnobis path. Supply whitening_matrix_W   # when Mahalanobis crossnobis distances are desired.   model_crossnobis <- contrast_rsa_model(       dataset = mvpa_dat,       design = msreve_des,       estimation_method = "crossnobis"   )   print(model_crossnobis) #>  #>  Contrast RSA Model Specification  #>  #> - Dataset  #>   - Class:  mvpa_image_dataset  #> - Design (`msreve_design`)  #>   - Name:  msreve_design_01  #>   - Contrast Matrix Dims:  4 Cond x 2 Contrasts  #>   - MVPA Design Class:  mvpa_design  #> - Analysis Parameters  #>   - Estimation Method (Uhat/d):  crossnobis  #>   - Whitening Matrix (W):  None (for Euclidean)  #>   - Regression Type (beta):  lm  #>   - Calc Reliability:      FALSE  #>   - Output Metric(s):       beta_delta  #>

code: labs <- c("faces","animals","plants","tools",           "vehicles","furniture","buildings","food")  # 1) Mini-DSL: 2x2 Factorial (Animacy x Size) + Interaction, Orthonormal C1 <- contrasts(         labels = labs,         spec   = ~ anim( faces + animals + plants + food ~ . )                  + size( faces + animals + tools + furniture ~ . )                  + anim:size,         orth   = TRUE) print(colnames(C1)) #> [1] "Orth1" "Orth2" "Orth3" print(attr(C1, "source")) #> [1] "anim"      "size"      "anim:size" print(round(crossprod(C1), 5)) #>       Orth1 Orth2 Orth3 #> Orth1     1     0     0 #> Orth2     0     1     0 #> Orth3     0     0     1  # 2) Mini-DSL: One-vs-rest, Centered, Unit Length (L2) C2 <- contrasts(labels = labs,                 spec   = ~ faces( faces ~ . ) + tools( tools ~ . ),                 scale = "l2") print(round(colSums(C2^2), 5)) # Should be 1 #> faces tools  #>     1     1   # 3) Metadata + Formula: Centered, Scaled (SD) meta <- tibble::tribble(   ~label,      ~anim, ~size,   "faces",        1,    0,   "animals",      1,    0,   "plants",       1,    1,   "tools",        0,    0,   "vehicles",     0,    1,   "furniture",    0,    0,   "buildings",    0,    1,   "food",         1,    1) # Note: labels argument is ignored here, order comes from meta$label # Also note: This function masks stats::contrasts C3 <- contrasts(metadata = meta,                 spec     = ~ anim + size + anim:size,                 scale    = "sd") print(round(colMeans(C3), 5)) # Should be 0 #>      anim      size anim:size  #>         0         0         0  print(round(apply(C3, 2, sd), 5)) # Should be 1 #>      anim      size anim:size  #>         1         1         1

title: Create a Feature-Based RSA Model — feature_rsa_model
text: Feature RSA models analyze well feature matrix F (defined `design`) relates neural data X. `max_comps` parameter, inherited `design` object, sets upper limit number components fitted:   - pls: PLS regression using configured pls numerical     kernel. Fits `max_comps` components; actual number used     prediction chosen ncomp_selection.   - pca: Principal Component Regression using configured     pls PCR kernel (SVD-PCR default). Fits `max_comps`     components; selection controlled ncomp_selection.   - ridge: Multi-response ridge regression using one economy SVD     per training matrix. distinct estimator, approximation     PLS elastic net. penalty selected lambda_selection.   - glmnet: Elastic net regression via glmnet multivariate Gaussian     response. Regularisation (lambda) can auto-selected via cv_glmnet=TRUE. pls pca, ncomp_selection argument determines many fitted components actually used prediction.  default ("loo") uses leave-one-observation-validation picks fewest components within one SE minimum segment-wise MSE. ncomp_objective = "mse" default retained backward compatibility. ncomp_selection = "blocked", callers may instead maximize "pattern_discrimination" "pattern_rank_percentile"; relative objectives default empirical optimum rather one-SE rule. "blocked" uses leave-one-block-segments within outer training fold, centering scaling estimated inner training split. usually faithful much less expensive validation unit observations dependent within acquisition runs, sessions, subjects. interchangeable "pve" "max", estimate held-performance component selection. **Performance Metrics** (computed `evaluate_model` cross-validation): *Condition-pattern metrics* (trial x trial correlation matrix):   - `pattern_correlation`: Average correlation predicted observed     spatial patterns corresponding trials (diagonal trial x trial     correlation matrix computed across voxels).   - `pattern_discrimination`: `pattern_correlation` minus mean     -diagonal correlation among candidates withheld outer     fold. Measures much better model predicts correct trial's     pattern eligible incorrect trials.   - `pattern_rank_percentile`: trial, percentile rank correct     pattern match among candidates withheld outer fold.     0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect. *Representational geometry*:   - `rdm_correlation`: Spearman correlation jointly withheld pairs     observed predicted RDMs (defined 1 - trial--trial     correlation across voxels). Captures similarity held-    representational geometry without comparing prediction target     trained prediction. *Global reconstruction metrics*:   - `voxel_correlation`: Correlation flattened predicted observed     matrices (trials x voxels).   - `mse`: Mean Squared Error.   - `r_squared`: 1 - RSS/TSS. *Voxel encoding fidelity*:   - `mean_voxelwise_temporal_cor`: Average per-voxel temporal correlation     predicted observed time courses. - `p_*`, `z_*`: `nperm > 0`, permutation-based p-values z-scores     metrics. PLS, PCR, glmnet, number components historical proxy (`ncomp`) included performance output. Ridge instead reports median selected penalty (`median_lambda`), mean effective degrees freedom (`mean_effective_df`), non-intercept degrees freedom, fractions folds selected either end lambda grid. **--fold predictions** (`return_predictions = TRUE`): ROI retains merged --fold `Yhat` `Y` matrices, observation order, outer-fold id used built-scoring rules. Extract feature_rsa_predictions post-hoc scoring (temporal windowing, whitened distances, custom identification rules) without crossing fold boundaries. different payload `return_rdm_vectors` classification `prediction_table`. Overlapping searchlights refused retain multiple copies voxel.

title: ITEM decoding model for ROI/searchlight analysis — item_model
text: Conceptually, ITEM differs archived `hrfdecoder` pathway decoder fit: - ITEM (`item_model`) first estimates trial-wise responses (`Gamma`) via LS-  performs covariance-aware decoding trial estimates. - archived `hrfdecoder` model fits continuous-time decoder directly   TR-level data aggregates TR predictions events afterward. Use ITEM want explicit trial-estimation stage direct control trial covariance handling (`U`), especially trial-level diagnostics. `return_predictions = TRUE` (default) full per-fold cross-validation payload retained every ROI result. searchlight schema combiner discards payload keeps scalar maps, `run_regional()` retains full results list; analyses many ROIs large trial counts, pass `return_predictions = FALSE` bound memory.

code: # Example feature matrix (4 conditions, 5 features) feat_mat <- matrix(rnorm(20), nrow = 4,                    dimnames = list(paste0("Cond", 1:4), paste0("F", 1:5)))  # Use raw features (first 3) C_raw <- make_feature_contrasts(feat_mat[, 1:3], use_pca = FALSE, prefix="RawFeat_") print(C_raw) #>        RawFeat_F1 RawFeat_F2 RawFeat_F3 #> Cond1  0.07690286 -0.6069563 -1.5540788 #> Cond2  0.55834935 -0.3955575  0.5245265 #> Cond3 -0.82182161  1.2180820 -0.3984093 #> Cond4 -0.36515220  0.6044720 -0.3807170  # Use PCA, selecting top 2 PCs C_pca <- make_feature_contrasts(feat_mat, use_pca = TRUE, n_pcs = 2, prefix="PCA_") print(C_pca) #>             PCA_PC1     PCA_PC2 #> Cond1  0.5348726259 -1.30373417 #> Cond2  1.2396494456  1.01259686 #> Cond3 -1.7747930122  0.31436180 #> Cond4  0.0002709406 -0.02322449  # Use PCA, selecting >= 80% variance explained C_pca_pve <- make_feature_contrasts(feat_mat, use_pca = TRUE, pve = 0.8, prefix="PCA_") print(C_pca_pve) #>             PCA_PC1     PCA_PC2 #> Cond1  0.5348726259 -1.30373417 #> Cond2  1.2396494456  1.01259686 #> Cond3 -1.7747930122  0.31436180 #> Cond4  0.0002709406 -0.02322449  # Reorder based on labels C_pca_reorder <- make_feature_contrasts(feat_mat, labels=c("Cond3", "Cond1", "Cond4", "Cond2"),                                       use_pca = TRUE, n_pcs = 2, prefix="PCA_") print(C_pca_reorder) #>             PCA_PC1     PCA_PC2 #> Cond3  1.7747930122 -0.31436180 #> Cond1 -0.5348726259  1.30373417 #> Cond4 -0.0002709406  0.02322449 #> Cond2 -1.2396494456 -1.01259686

text: mod_spec MVPA model specification object containing dataset analyze, compute_performance (logical indicating whether compute performance metrics), return_predictions (logical indicating whether return predictions). vox_list list voxel indices coordinates defining ROI analyze. ids Vector identifiers ROI analysis. Defaults 1:length(vox_list). batch_size Integer specifying number ROIs process per batch. Searchlight analyses use memory-aware automatic size based sphere size, observation count, worker count, backend; shard batches larger carry indices rather extracted ROI matrices. regional analyses default ROIs one batch, unless estimated extraction memory exceed budget set options(rMVPA.regional_mem_budget) (default 2 GB), case batches automatically sized stay within budget. verbose Logical indicating whether print progress messages. Defaults TRUE. TRUE progressr package installed, real-time progress bar shown updates ROI completes – even running parallel future workers. Without progressr, coarse batch-level log messages printed. Install install.packages("progressr") activate per session progressr::handlers(global = TRUE). processor Optional custom processing function. NULL, uses default processor. Must accept parameters (obj, roi, rnum) return tibble. analysis_type Character indicating type analysis. Defaults "searchlight". drop_probs Logical; TRUE, drop per-ROI probability matrices computing metrics. Default FALSE. fail_fast Logical; TRUE, stop immediately first ROI error. code: mod <- load_model("sda") arr_data <- array(rnorm(6*6*6*100), c(6,6,6,100)) sp <- neuroim2::NeuroSpace(c(6,6,6,100)) traindat <- neuroim2::NeuroVec(arr_data, sp) mask <- neuroim2::LogicalNeuroVol(array(rnorm(6*6*6)>-.2, c(6,6,6)), neuroim2::NeuroSpace(c(6,6,6)))  mvdset <- mvpa_dataset(traindat,mask=mask) design <- data.frame(fac=rep(letters[1:4], 25), block=rep(1:10, each=10)) cval <- blocked_cross_validation(design$block) mvdes <- mvpa_design(design, y_train = ~ fac, block_var = ~ block)  custom_perf <- function(result) {   c(accuracy=sum(result$observed == result$predicted)/length(result$observed)) } mvpmod <- mvpa_model(mod, dataset=mvdset, design=mvdes, crossval=cval, performance=custom_perf) print(mvpmod) #> mvpa_model object.  #> model:  sda  #> model type:  classification  #>  #>  Blocked Cross-Validation  #>  #> - Dataset Information  #>   - Observations:  100  #>   - Number of Folds:  10  #> - Block Information  #>   - Total Blocks:  10  #>   - Mean Block Size:  10  (SD:  0 )  #>   - Block Sizes:  1: 10, 2: 10, 3: 10, 4: 10, 5: 10, 6: 10, 7: 10, 8: 10, 9: 10, 10: 10  #>  #>  #>  MVPA Dataset  #>  #> - Training Data  #>   - Dimensions:  6 x 6 x 6 x 100 observations  #>   - Type:  DenseNeuroVec  #> - Test Data  #>   -  None  #> - Mask Information  #>   - Areas:  TRUE : 118  #>   - Active voxels/vertices:  118  #>  #>  #>  MVPA Design  #>  #> - Training Data  #>   - Observations:  100  #>   - Response Type:  Factor #>   - Levels:  a, b, c, d  #>   - Class Distribution:  a: 25, b: 25, c: 25, d: 25  #> - Test Data  #>   -  None  #> - Structure  #>   - Blocking:  Present #>   - Number of Blocks:  10  #>   - Mean Block Size:  10  (SD:  0 )  #>   - Split Groups:  None  #>
